# Documentation Index

Index for discovering relevant documents during Plan and Explore execution

## Usage

Identify and read task-related sections below:

- Modify `cmd/` or CLI behavior → Read **Specifications** section (CLI, Requirements)
- Modify YAML configuration handling → Read **Specifications** section (Configuration, Requirements)
- Make design decisions or evaluate scope → Read **Project Overview** section
- Edit documents under `docs/` → Read **Contributing** section
- Modify the release workflow, `.goreleaser.yaml`, or `Dockerfile` → Read **Contributing** section (Release Workflow)
- Change explanations for users → Read **User Guide** section and **Contributing** section (Documentation Policy)

## Specifications

- [Requirements](docs/spec/requirements.md): Functional requirements, quality requirements, and invariants of reco - Use when implementing or changing features, or checking supported scope and safety guarantees
- [CLI](docs/spec/cli.md): Commands (`plan`, `apply`, `show`), options, credential selection (`GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN`, the `gh auth token` premise, and the Admin role as the verified condition), interactive approval, and the user-visible output: `plan` lines (`<current> -> <desired>`, related resources with `absent` / `present` and quoted variable values, `(environment absent)` and other parenthesized states for values that cannot be read, `Patterns to remove:` / `Patterns to add:`, and the `Applicability:`, `Previous settings:`, and `Side effect:` lines, whose conditions are left to the settings design), display order and counts, `apply` result words (`updated`, `failed`, `not attempted`, `no change`) with `Update request`, `Desired state`, `Precondition:`, `Other settings:`, `Possible cause:`, and `Note:` lines, `show` output in the same YAML structure as the configuration file (unreadable values and absent kinds as comments, variable values shown unmasked), stdout vs. stderr, the one-line JSON error, redirect errors, and exit codes - Use when modifying `cmd/`, adding commands or options, or changing user-visible output and exit codes
- [Configuration](docs/spec/configuration.md): YAML configuration structure, types, allowed values, combinations, what each declaration means, and input validation; omitted settings stay unmanaged, and a valid declaration may still be found not applicable after observation, as the settings design defines. `general` with the three merge methods (`allow_squash_merge`, `allow_merge_commit`, `allow_rebase_merge`, independent booleans with all three `false` rejected) and `allow_update_branch`, `actions.permissions` with `enabled`, `allowed_actions` (which includes Actions being enabled), the three `selected_actions` items as one group, `patterns_allowed` as a set, and `sha_pinning_required`, `actions.access.access_level` (`organization` rejected), related-resource declarations including `actions.variables` (names limited to upper-case ASCII letters, digits, and underscores, not starting with a digit or `GITHUB_`, lower case rejected with the upper-case spelling, values required to be non-empty strings with unquoted numbers and booleans rejected with a quoting hint, no trimming, and `state: absent` instead of `value` declaring a variable to delete, with `state` accepting only `absent`, `state` with `value` rejected, and a missing or null `value` never read as a deletion), `environments` (names limited to printable ASCII and compared ignoring ASCII letter case, `deployment_branch_policy.mode` and the `patterns` set required only for `selected`, and `variables` with the same rules as `actions.variables`, duplicates checked per environment, an environment with only `variables` still declared to exist, and same-named Repository Variables kept separate), `security` with `dependabot_alerts` and `dependabot_security_updates` (independent booleans, `false` with `true` rejected, a paused security update matching `true`), `secret_scanning` and `secret_scanning_push_protection` with the same rule, and `private_vulnerability_reporting`, the last three managed only on public repositories, and YAML-level validation (keys, booleans, null, anchors, tags, encoding, repository names and duplicates) - Use when modifying configuration parsing or validation, or adding supported repository settings

## Design

- [Domain Model](docs/design/domain.md): Core concepts of reco and the distinctions between them that hold for every setting (declaration, selection, and repository identity; management units vs. managed settings; desired values that include the state of another unit vs. dependent settings and their prerequisite settings; setting values shared across contexts, including equal values with different representations; side effects, settings without side effect, and resumed settings; current state vs. observation result and the points in time of observation; reading a failure response as a value only when no other interpretation remains; reconciliation vs. applicability; change plan structure; logical change vs. update operation; approval, change preconditions, and the anticipated value each update operation is checked against; related resources, their existence (a list with two resources of the same name failing the observation), creation, deletion only by declared absence, comparable names and names whose identity cannot be determined (never arising for Variables), the shared representation of a related resource's existence (with a value for value-carrying kinds) or absence as a setting value, with IDs compared separately, and identity; set-valued settings whose added and removed elements are parts of one planned change; changes of related resources with different names as separate logical changes, a creation checked for absence even where GitHub would reject a duplicate, and a value change never replaced by a creation; the contexts each concept belongs to) - Use when naming domain types, deciding what a concept means, or checking that code keeps these distinctions
- [Architecture](docs/design/architecture.md): Logical components and their boundaries, package layout, change planning and execution control, pre-validation, the repository read sent first and the order of setting areas, the acquisition contract, the update contract for normal responses whose body is or is not a resource representation, related-resource list pagination and completeness checks, per-resource reads sent only to the related resources a `plan` / `apply` observation names, the per-list page size, response body limit, and page limit, raised only for lists whose maximum page size follows from GitHub's limits, the policy for treating changes as not applicable, approval and per-update precondition checks, GitHub API trust boundary (redirects, unmanaged-setting preservation, non-atomic updates and intermediate states), result classification, re-observation, and the interval between update requests - Use when placing responsibilities across packages, implementing the plan/apply flow, or changing a mechanism shared by every setting
- [Settings Design](docs/design/settings/README.md): How setting-specific design is split by top-level configuration key and the common section structure of each document (settings and management units, observation, applicability and side effects, logical changes and update operations, update method, scenarios) - Use when adding a supported setting or deciding where a setting-specific rule belongs
- [General Design](docs/design/settings/general.md): `general` settings (the repository `GET` that every observation sends first, merge-related fields missing below the Write role as a failure, a change disabling a merge method not applicable when every merge method would end up disabled, with the undeclared disabled ones named in the reason and not added to the change preconditions, the merge method changes bundled into one logical change sent as one `PATCH` so that swapping the enabled method never passes through all disabled, `allow_update_branch` updated on its own, the `private` and `permissions` fields of that response, the partial `PATCH` and the Secret scanning settings compared after it) - Use when changing how `general` is read or updated
- [Actions Design](docs/design/settings/actions.md): `actions` settings (Actions permissions, selected actions, `sha_pinning_required`, workflow permissions, access from outside workflows, and Repository Variables read from the list with a page size, body limit, and page limit derived from GitHub's limits, with an empty value as an existing variable and duplicate names as a contract violation, matched by name ignoring ASCII case, planned as a creation, a value change, or a deletion for `state: absent` that is always applicable, applied one variable per logical change by a `POST` with the name and value, a value-only `PATCH`, or a body-less `DELETE`, with the variable's absence or planned value checked before the update, `409` on creation and `404` on deletion treated as a rejected update, a deletion completed only when the list lacks the name, and other variables not compared; their read requests and unavailability conditions, the allowed-actions transition table and intermediate state, applicability of `sha_pinning_required` and `access_level`, resumed settings, the fields each `PUT` sends and the settings compared after it) - Use when changing how GitHub Actions settings are read, planned, or updated
- [Environments Design](docs/design/settings/environments.md): `environments` (environment names matched beyond ASCII case and the not-applicable case it causes, the environment list always read in full, the patterns of `selected` environments and Environment Variables (a separate area read after the patterns with a 4-page limit and duplicates checked per environment, by `plan` / `apply` only when declared) read from every listed environment by `show` but only from the environments a `plan` / `apply` observation names, matched as the same name and never an undetermined one, with unread patterns kept distinct from an empty set, planned right after their environment, applied one variable per logical change after the environment's creation completes, based on the environment's ID and the variable for an existing environment and only on the variable's absence for a created one, a `state: absent` variable of an environment to create added to the creation's desired state without an update, with no unmanaged settings compared, the creation and deployment branch policy transition table with the mode `PUT`, a `DELETE` per removed pattern, then a `POST` per added pattern, the anticipated pattern set after each update, and `303` on a duplicate pattern treated as an unknown outcome) - Use when changing how environments and their deployment branch policies are read, planned, or updated
- [Security Design](docs/design/settings/security.md): `security` settings (Dependabot alerts read as `204` enabled and `404` disabled only when `permissions.admin` is true, Dependabot security updates with `paused`, Secret scanning and repository push protection read from `security_and_analysis` and unavailable on private repositories, private vulnerability reporting read only on public repositories; dependent and prerequisite settings, the dependency graph side effect, applicability, execution order, and updates by a nested one-item `PATCH` or an empty `PUT` / `DELETE`) - Use when changing how security settings are read, planned, or updated

## Research

- [Research](docs/research/README.md): Purpose of the GitHub API research documents, how they are split, and the conventions they follow (grounded only in GitHub official docs, API version basis, developer-verified behavior as notes) - Use when adding a GitHub API fact or a new endpoint document
- [GitHub OpenAPI Excerpt](docs/research/openapi.json): Excerpt of GitHub's official OpenAPI 3.0 description limited to the operations reco uses and the components they reference, generated by `scripts/openapi/update.sh` - Use when checking request or response field types and enum values of an endpoint reco uses
- [GitHub REST API Common](docs/research/rest-api.md): GitHub REST API contract shared by every endpoint reco uses (request URL and headers, API versions, redirects, failure responses, rate limits, conditional requests, token types, scopes, and repository roles) - Use when a spec or design needs a GitHub fact that is not specific to one endpoint
- [GitHub Repositories API](docs/research/repositories.md): Repository get and update endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, merge-related field visibility, repository name vs. ID and rename redirects, general setting fields (including the three merge methods and `allow_update_branch`) and update behavior, with `422` when every merge method would be disabled, and the settings-screen items they correspond to; security settings: `security_and_analysis` with nested `PATCH` preservation and secret scanning / push protection dependencies, Dependabot alerts whose `DELETE` also disables the dependency graph and security updates (no REST operation reads the dependency graph state or changes it alone), Dependabot security updates with `paused` and `422` while alerts are off, and private vulnerability reporting, with observed private-repository responses) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about repository identity, general settings, or the security settings on the repositories page
- [GitHub Actions Permissions API](docs/research/actions-permissions.md): Actions permissions, selected actions, workflow permissions, and access from workflows outside the repository endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, fields, update units, observed side effects, and the settings-screen items they correspond to) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about GitHub Actions permission settings
- [GitHub Actions Variables API](docs/research/actions-variables.md): Repository and environment variable list, get, create, update, and delete endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses including `409` on an existing name and `404` for a missing variable or environment, observed private-repository availability, names stored in upper case and compared ignoring case, the 300-character name and 48,000-byte value limits, empty values rejected and other values returned as sent, list pagination capped at 30 per page with `total_count` and completeness, elements without IDs matching the individual get, page sizes beyond 1 MiB with large values, environment names in the path, and other variables and environments unchanged by each operation) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about GitHub Actions variables
- [GitHub Deployment Environments API](docs/research/deployment-environments.md): Environment list, get, and create-or-update endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses, plan and repository-visibility availability with observed private-repository behavior, name case-insensitivity (also accents, full-width letters, trailing spaces, and control characters) and URL encoding, list pagination and completeness, environment IDs, the `deployment_branch_policy` representation, field preservation on `PUT`, and the loss of branch patterns when the policy type changes) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about deployment environments
- [GitHub Deployment Branch Policies API](docs/research/deployment-branch-policies.md): Deployment branch and tag pattern list, get, create, and delete endpoints (required permissions, HTTP responses including `404` when custom policies are off and `303` for duplicates, pattern type and case-sensitive names, pagination, and IDs changing on recreation) - Use when a spec or design needs a fact about an environment's deployment branch and tag patterns

## User Guide

- [User Guide](docs/user-guide/README.md): Entry point of the user guide for reco users, not implementers (intended readers and the documents to read for each user goal, split into main documents and optional detail documents) - Use when choosing which user-facing document to read or adding a new one
- [Overview](docs/user-guide/overview.md): What reco solves and whether it fits the reader, for users evaluating adoption (the problem it addresses, the declare / `plan` / `apply` flow and `show`, the settings it manages described by what they control and mapped to GitHub settings-screen items) - Use when explaining what reco is and whether it suits a user's needs, or when changing supported settings or scope that this summary repeats
- [Configuration Guide](docs/user-guide/configuration.md): How to write the configuration file for users (file location and structure, tables of keys, allowed values, and meanings for `general` (including the merge methods, which cannot all be disabled, and `allow_update_branch`, which does not update branches automatically), `actions.permissions`, `actions.workflow`, `actions.access`, `actions.variables` (upper-case names, quoting values that look like numbers, unwritten variables left untouched, deleting a variable by writing `state: absent` instead of removing its line, values shown in output, `apply` creating, updating, and deleting them), `environments` (including `selected` with its `patterns` list, which `apply` makes GitHub match, and `environments[].variables` written like `actions.variables`), and `security` (Dependabot alerts and security updates, and what disabling alerts also disables; Secret scanning and repository push protection on public repositories, and what disabling Secret scanning also disables; private vulnerability reporting on public repositories) with the points to watch when writing them, unwritten settings staying unmanaged, listing multiple repositories, common mistakes) - Use when explaining to users how to declare settings, or when changing configuration behavior that users rely on
- [Safety Guide](docs/user-guide/safety.md): Optional detail document on how reco keeps changes safe, in plain user-facing terms (not changing unwritten settings, deleting only variables written with `state: absent` and not when their value changed after approval, reading every repository before updating, changing only what was approved, stopping when settings change after approval or a problem occurs, confirming the result before reporting completion, keeping the token out of output while showing Repository Variables values, and what reco does not do such as rollback, retry, or following redirects) - Use when explaining reco's safety behavior to users, or when changing an invariant or behavior that users rely on for trust
- [Command Reference](docs/user-guide/commands.md): Commands, options, and their defaults for users (`show`, `plan`, `apply`; `show` printing Repository Variables values to stdout so secrets belong in Secrets; `--repo` takes one repository, which for `plan` / `apply` must be declared in the configuration file; example output of each command and how to read the plan lines (including environment creation `absent -> present`, Repository and Environment Variable lines with quoted values and `"<value>" -> absent` / `(environment absent) -> absent` for `state: absent`, `Patterns to remove:` / `Patterns to add:`, `Side effect:`, `Applicability: not applicable`, and `Plan cannot be applied.`) and the `apply` result words; what `apply` does and when it asks for approval, which only `y` or `yes` on a terminal grants; `GH_TOKEN` / `GITHUB_TOKEN` selection; stdout vs. stderr and the one-line JSON error; exit code `0` on success and `1` on failure, including `plan` with a change that cannot be applied) - Use when explaining commands, options, approval, or exit codes to users, or when changing CLI behavior that users script against
- [Installation](docs/user-guide/installation.md): Installing and running reco for users (GitHub Releases binaries installed with copy-paste curl commands per OS and architecture, a first `show` with `GH_TOKEN`, and pulling the GHCR image by a version tag and running `plan` in a mounted working directory) - Use when explaining how to install or run reco, or when changing distribution or image behavior that users rely on
- [Authentication](docs/user-guide/authentication.md): Preparing the token for users (passing `gh auth token` output in `GH_TOKEN`, what `gh auth login` / `gh auth token` do, token permissions not exceeding the owner's role, passing a token of an account with the Admin role, roles below Write failing, roles below Admin failing for Dependabot and Secret scanning settings, and private vulnerability reporting readable below Admin but changeable only with Admin) - Use when explaining which token and role reco needs, or when changing credential behavior that users rely on
- [Verification](docs/user-guide/verification.md): Optional verification of downloads for advanced users (`gh attestation verify` for binaries and the container image via `container-image.txt`, why `SHA256SUMS` alone is not enough, running the verified image by digest) - Use when explaining how to verify release artifacts, or when changing the release workflow's attestation
- [Getting Started](docs/user-guide/getting-started.md): Tutorial that walks a user through one setting on one repository (`show`, writing `reco.yaml` with `general.delete_branch_on_merge`, `plan`, approving `apply`, confirming `No changes.`, and reverting by declaring the old value) - Use when explaining the first use of reco, or when changing output or behavior that the first run shows
- [Operations](docs/user-guide/operations.md): Procedures for managing multiple repositories (adding a repository after checking it with `show` and applying only it with `--repo`, narrowing a run to one repository, ordering repositories since updates follow the file order and stop at the first incomplete repository, periodic `plan` to notice drift, reverting values, and stopping management by removing lines or repositories, with variables deleted by `state: absent` before their lines are removed) - Use when explaining day-to-day use of reco across repositories, or when changing selection, ordering, or stop behavior that these procedures rely on
- [Troubleshooting](docs/user-guide/troubleshooting.md): What to do after an error or an unexpected `apply` result, organized by symptom (reading the one-line JSON error; a missing configuration file, configuration mistakes, an undeclared `--repo`, a missing or invalid token, insufficient role (`403` / `404` / missing fields), `Plan cannot be applied.` with how to read the reason and fix the declaration (on private repositories, removing the key the reason names), approval not available or declined, an `apply` that stopped partway with the meaning of `Update request` and `Desired state` (including several `Update request (...)` lines for pattern updates), auto-merge not applied on GitHub Free private repositories, and a table of rarer errors and lines such as rate limits, `redirect not followed` (including `303` when a pattern already exists), `409` / `404` / `422` on variable updates, `Precondition:`, and `Other settings:`) - Use when explaining to users how to recover from errors or partial results, or when changing error messages or result lines that users act on

## Project Overview

- [Constitution](docs/CONSTITUTION.md): Purpose, problem statement, value proposition, design principles, and non-goals of reco - Use when making design decisions, resolving tradeoffs between principles, or judging whether a feature is in scope

## Contributing

- [Documentation Policy](docs/contributing/docs-policy.md): Responsibilities and sources of truth of each document, what the requirements document, the CLI spec, and the configuration spec contain and what they leave to the other documents, the split of design documents by what change triggers each (concepts and shared mechanisms in the domain model and architecture, setting-specific rules in the settings design), identifiers (`FR`, `QR`, `INV`), Relationships (`alignment`, `grounding`, `checks`) including the one-line `//trace:checks` declaration on top-level test functions, consistency checks on change, checking with `sdlc validate --config sdlc.yaml` and finding references with `sdlc trace`, the split of readers (implementers for most of `docs/`, reco users for `docs/user-guide/`), and the rules for the user guide (readers, relation to the specifications, writing rules on caveats, terms, links, and duplication, main vs. detail documents, checks when changing documents, output examples) - Use when adding or changing requirements, identifiers, or Relationship tables, when editing specs and designs, or when editing the user guide
- [Release Workflow](docs/contributing/release.md): Tag-triggered release to GitHub Releases and GHCR (job order and permissions, artifacts, build settings, container image, provenance attestation, partial publication and re-runs, user-side verification, pinning of actions and tools) - Use when modifying `.github/workflows/release.yml`, `.goreleaser.yaml`, or `Dockerfile`, or when cutting a release
